questions.q: What did Jonathan say his father did not do without telling him?
questions.a: He said that his father did nothing either great or small without revealing it to him.

questions.q: How close did David say he was to death?
questions.a: He said that there was only a step between him and death.

questions.q: What did David ask Jonathan to let him do until the third evening?
questions.a: David asked to hide in the field until the third evening.

questions.q: What reason did David tell Jonathan to give Saul if Saul missed him?
questions.a: He was to tell Saul that David had asked make a brief visit to his city, Bethlehem, for the yearly sacrifice for his whole clan.

questions.q: Why did David ask Jonathan to deal faithfully with him?
questions.a: David asked this because Jonathan had brought him into a covenant of Yahweh.

questions.q: Where did Jonathan ask David to go so they could talk?
questions.a: He asked David to go with him out into the field so they could speak privately.

questions.q: Why did Jonathan want to make his father’s intentions known to David?
questions.a: Jonathan promised to reveal his father’s intentions so that David flee.

questions.q: How did Jonathan know that David would keep his promise that he would not harm Jonathan’s descendants?
questions.a: Jonathan knew that David would keep that promise because David loved Jonathan as much as he loved himself.

questions.q: Whom did Jonathan say he would send to find the arrows he shot?
questions.a: He said he would send a boy to find the arrows.

questions.q: When the festival of the new moon came, what did the king do?
questions.a: The king came to the table for the feast.

questions.q: What did Saul think might have happened to David to make him absent from the feast?
questions.a: Saul thought it was an accident and that David was not ritually clean.

questions.q: Why did Jonathan say David had to attend his family’s sacrifice?
questions.a: He said David’s brother had commanded him to be there.

questions.q: What did Saul call his son Jonathan in his burning anger?
questions.a: He called him the son a mother who must have been unfaithful to Saul, because no real son of his would have done that.

questions.q: Why was Jonathan grieved for David?
questions.a: He was grieved for David because his father had dishonored him, saying unfairly that David was not loyal to him.

questions.q: Where did Jonathan shoot an arrow as the boy ran?
questions.a: Jonathan shot an arrow over the boy so that it would land on the ground far ahead of him.

questions.q: What did Jonathan do after David left?
questions.a: Jonathan went back into the city of Gibeah.

commentary.text: Saul, missing David, seeks to kill Jonathan.

Verses 1–10 The trials David met with, prepared him for future advancement. Thus the Lord deals with those whom he prepares unto glory. He does not put them into immediate possession of the kingdom, but leads them to it through much tribulation, which he makes the means of fitting them for it. Let them not murmur at his gracious appointment, nor distrust his care; but let them look forward with joyful expectation to the crown which is laid up for them. Sometimes it appears to us that there is but a step between us and death; at all times it may be so, and we should prepare for the event. But though dangers appear most threatening, we cannot die till the purpose of God concerning us is accomplished; nor till we have served our generation according to his will, if we are believers. Jonathan generously offers David his services. This is true friendship. Thus Christ testifies his love to us, Ask, and it shall be done for you; and we must testify our love to him, by keeping his commandments.

Jonathan faithfully promises that he would let David know how he found his father affected towards him. It will be kindness to ourselves and to ours, to secure an interest in those whom God favours, and to make his friends ours. True friendship rests on a firm basis, and is able to silence ambition, self-love, and undue regard for others. But who can fully understand the love of Jesus, who gave himself as a sacrifice for rebellious, polluted sinners! how great then ought to be the force and effects of our love to him, to his cause, and his people!

None were more constant than David in attending holy duties; nor had he been absent, but self-preservation obliged him to withdraw. In great peril present opportunities for Divine ordinances may be waved. But it is bad for us, except in case of necessity, to omit any opportunity of statedly attending on them. Jonathan did wisely and well for himself and family, to secure an interest in David, yet for this he is blamed. It is good to take God's people for our people. It will prove to our advantage at last, however it may now be thought against our interest. Saul was outrageous. What savage beasts, and worse, does anger make men!

The separation of two such faithful friends was grievous to both, but David's case was the more deplorable, for David was leaving all his comforts, even those of God's sanctuary. Christians need not sorrow, as men without hope; but being one with Christ, they are one with each other, and will meet in his presence ere long, to part no more; to meet where all tears shall be wiped from their eyes.
